core.title: Declare journeys as topology above interlockings: entrypoint, continuations, explicit terminals
core.given: A journey document composing routing decisions across interlockings, each interlocking selecting exactly one linear train
core.when: the planner authors or changes the journey's entrypoint, routes, continuations or terminals
core.then: Declare the journey as {station-entrypoint, entrypoint-interlocking, route-continuations, explicit-terminals}: if exposed, its starting actions on the consumer-facing start surface (stack name via profile: idiom.journey_start_surface), its consumer surfaces and first interlocking; and for every route, after its selected train completes, either an explicit terminal or a continuation from (interlocking_id, route_id) via a named artifact that train produces to the next interlocking.
prefer: Compose interlocking -> train -> interlocking; keep each interlocking a local boundary selecting one linear train.
Ownership: the interlocking selects the train, the train executor (stack component via profile: idiom.train_executor) executes wagons linearly, the journey owns continuation.

Exposed journeys: the stack binds the declared start-surface actions (profile: idiom.journey_start_surface) to the journey entry through its entry-binding idiom (profile: idiom.journey_entry_binding).
Treat journey artifacts as planner data; a separate runtime may introduce a journey executor (stack component via profile: idiom.journey_executor).
avoid: Recursive interlockings (one selecting or invoking another).
Moving wagon execution out of the train executor (stack component via profile: idiom.train_executor), or letting any of the three absorb the others.
Implicitly dangling routes, or continuations not keyed by an artifact the selected train produces.
Encoding runtime execution (e.g. a journey executor, profile: idiom.journey_executor) into the semantic journey definition.
core.why: Keeping continuation in the journey lets routing compose across interlockings without recursive interlockings or split wagon execution, so each boundary stays local and verifiable.
evidence: The journey document validates against the stack's canonical journey schema (profile: layout.journey_schema).
Exposed journeys list start-surface actions (stack name via profile: idiom.journey_start_surface) / consumer surfaces and an entrypoint interlocking.
Every (interlocking_id, route_id) reached by the journey has either an explicit terminal or a continuation naming an artifact produced by that route's selected train and a target interlocking.
No interlocking selects another interlocking; wagon execution remains in the train executor (stack component via profile: idiom.train_executor).
verification: Journey shape check: journey -> {station-entrypoint, entrypoint-interlocking, route-continuations, explicit-terminals}; journey documents are validated against the stack's canonical journey schema (profile: layout.journey_schema).
continuation = binding from one (interlocking_id, route_id) pair, through an artifact produced by that route's selected train, to the next interlocking.
terminal = explicit declaration that a route ends the journey rather than continuing to another interlocking.

station_entrypoint: exposed journeys declare start-surface actions (stack name via profile: idiom.journey_start_surface) and consumer surfaces; the stack binds those actions to the journey entry through its entry-binding idiom (profile: idiom.journey_entry_binding); the concrete stack rule that performs the binding is realization detail and stays with the realization.

values: journey document (the plan-artifact kind validated against the stack's canonical journey schema, profile: layout.journey_schema)
consumer start surface (stack name via profile: idiom.journey_start_surface)
wagon execution placed outside the train executor (stack component via profile: idiom.train_executor)

fires: Planner adds a new journey that should be startable from actions on the consumer-facing start surface (profile: idiom.journey_start_surface).
Planner adds a route to an interlocking used by a journey and must decide whether the route terminates or continues.
Planner wants control to pass to another interlocking after a selected train finishes producing an artifact.
A plan proposes making an interlocking select another interlocking, or making a journey run wagons directly.
doesNotFire: Planner edits only a single interlocking's train selection without touching any journey continuation or terminal.
Planner edits only wagon order inside one linear train.
Work on a journey-executor runtime implementation (stack component via profile: idiom.journey_executor; governed by runtime conventions, not this semantic definition).

proposedKeys.meaning: Path of the canonical schema that defines the shape of the journey plan artifact, against which journey documents are validated.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The layout group covers where artifacts are placed and the urn group covers identifier shapes; no existing key locates a plan artifact's canonical validation schema, which this rule's activation, evidence and shape check all defer to.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's concrete name for the consumer-facing start surface whose actions start an exposed journey.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers handlers, auth, errors, validation, gates and markup constructs, and roles.* describe file roles; no existing key names the start surface from which an exposed journey is launched, which the entrypoint obligation, activation task terms and the station_entrypoint check all need.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's component that executes a selected train's wagons linearly.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing idiom key names the linear train-execution component; the ownership statements (prefer[1], avoid[1]), evidence[3] and the ownership-boundary finding all refer to it, so its concrete name is reusable stack idiom rather than Bun-only content.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's runtime component that may execute a journey, deliberately kept separate from the semantic journey definition.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing idiom key names a runtime journey-execution component; roles.* cover architectural file roles, not runtime component names, yet prefer[3], the avoid[3] example and the runtime-work exclusion in activation all refer to the executor generically.

proposedKeys.meaning: How the stack binds each declared start-surface action to the journey entry (the concrete binding target and shape).
proposedKeys.bunValue: binds the declared Station Master actions to {journeyId, path}
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.binding.journey describes a source or test file binding itself to a journey artifact by URN syntax; the entry binding instead routes consumer start-surface actions to a journey entry ({journeyId, path}) and is realized by a separate stack rule, so no existing key fits.

bunOnly.reason: References the Bun coder rule that realizes the entry binding; a concrete stack's rule id is realization detail. The binding shape {journeyId, path} itself is profile data (idiom.journey_entry_binding), and the start surface name is profile data (idiom.journey_start_surface).
Names the ATDD-Bun runtime realization; the core says only 'a separate runtime', and the executor component name comes from idiom.journey_executor.

bunOnly.text: Bun binds those actions via coder.bun.station-master-journey-routing
bunOnly.reason: Same split as prefer[2]: the stack qualifier and the Bun coder-rule reference are realization details with no stack-neutral equivalent; the surface name and the {journeyId, path} binding shape are carried by idiom.journey_start_surface and idiom.journey_entry_binding.

neutralityNotes: The planner-topology vocabulary (journey, interlocking, train, wagon, route, continuation, terminal, entrypoint) is treated as stack-neutral ATDD planning vocabulary, since the profile vocabulary itself recognizes train, wagon and journey artifacts. The stack-specific component and surface names are reusable stack-idiom values, not obligations exclusive to one realization: 'Station Master' (idiom.journey_start_surface), 'TrainRunner' (idiom.train_executor), 'JourneyRunner' (idiom.journey_executor) and the {journeyId, path} entry-binding shape (idiom.journey_entry_binding) are carried as proposed profile keys and referenced consistently in the core obligation, activation facts/fires/exclusions and the verification entries; the closed vocabulary had no fitting keys, so all are proposed. What could not be made neutral: (1) the reference to the coder rule coder.bun.station-master-journey-routing, a concrete stack's rule id that realizes the entry binding (stays with the realization, per notProfileKeys; the core verification describes the check generically and without naming the stack); (2) the 'Bun runtime' qualifier in prefer[3], which names the reference realization (core says only 'a separate runtime'); (3) the canonical journey schema path is data, not rule text, carried by the proposed layout.journey_schema key.
